  Draft Historic Preservation Ordinance

TO:  City of Alhambra Historic Preservation Commission

FROM:  Andrew Ho, Director of Community Development
  Vanessa Reynoso, Deputy Director of Community Development
  By: Maia McCurley, Principal Planner

SUBJECT:  Draft Historic Preservation Ordinance

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY:

Following a two-month public review period for the Draft Historic Preservation Ordinance and a
concurrent outreach process involving community meetings and a questionnaire, the Historic
Preservation Commission is reconvening to consider and discuss the Draft Historic Preservation
Ordinance (“Discussion Draft”), as well as the community feedback that has been received to
date. During the meeting, it is expected that direction will be provided on how the Historic
Preservation Commission wishes to proceed with the Draft Historic Preservation Ordinance.
Based on the direction given, City staff and the City’s consultant will move forward with the
necessary steps for the Historic Preservation Commission to make a formal recommendation to
the Planning Commission and City Council at their next regular meeting.

BACKGROUND:

Since the Historic Preservation Commission last convened, the Draft Historic Preservation
Ordinance, also referred to as the “Discussion Draft,” was released for review on September 26,
2024 (Attachment 1). On the same day, a questionnaire was also made available to solicit the
community’s opinions and input on the development of a Historic Preservation Ordinance
(Attachment 2). Following the release of the Draft Historic Preservation Ordinance and the
questionnaire, five (5) City Council District community meetings were held on the following dates:

   October 2, 2024 (Council District 5)
   October 9, 2024 (Council District 3)
   October 15, 2024 (Council District 4)
   October 30, 2024 (Council District 2)
   November 6, 2024 (Council District 1)

The community meetings and the questionnaire were advertised through the City’s social media
accounts, the project website (www.HistoricAlhambra.com), e-mails to the City’s Historic
Preservation Program mailing list, and through three (3) separate direct mailings totaling 8,948
letters and flyers to property owners and occupants of both properties identified in the City-wide
Historic Resources Survey as potentially eligible historic resources or as being located within
potentially eligible historic districts.

Three (3) of the community meetings were held on Zoom and two (2) of the community meetings
were held in-person. Peak attendance at each of the meetings varied but ranged from
approximately 15 to 70 people. Each meeting was hosted by the respective Council Member for

 that district and featured the same presentation by the City’s consultant, Historic Resources
Group (“HRG”). The presentation covered the City’s Historic Preservation Program efforts thus
far, including the Historic Context Statement and the Citywide Historic Resources Survey, and an
overview of Historic Preservation Ordinances. During each presentation attendees were asked to
participate in informal polls intended to gauge their initial opinions on the development of a Historic
Preservation Ordinance. The eight (8) questions utilized during the informal polls were the same
questions included on the questionnaire, and attendees were encouraged to complete a
questionnaire after the meeting to provide their formal input. After the presentation portion, each
meeting also featured an opportunity to discuss questions from attendees. The presentation slides
and recordings of each community meeting are available for review on the project website:
www.HistoricAlhambra.com.

The Historic Preservation Ordinance questionnaire, which consisted of multiple-choice questions,
was available for more than seven (7) weeks with a deadline to submit completed questionnaires
on November 18, 2024. Copies of the questionnaire were available at City Hall and at the two (2)
in-person community meetings, in addition to being available both as an online form and in PDF
format on the project website. Questionnaires were also mailed directly to 3,017 property owners
and occupants of properties identified in the City-wide Historic Resources Survey as potentially
eligible historic resources or as contributors/non-contributors of a potentially eligible historic
district. In total, 235 completed questionnaires were received from unique individuals. Of these
completed questionnaires, approximately 168 of the responses were from property owners and
occupants of properties identified as potentially eligible historic resources or located within
potentially eligible historic districts. The results of the feedback received from the questionnaire
will be presented in further detail by HRG as part of their overall presentation for the December
4th Historic Preservation Commission meeting. The results, while not statistically valid, provide a
snapshot of the community’s thoughts and opinions, which is intended to help inform the
ordinance development process.

As the community has participated in community meetings, completed questionnaires, and
reviewed the Draft Historic Preservation Ordinance, several inquiries, comments, and questions
have been submitted. To respond to these questions and comments, an updated FAQ was
incorporated into the project website to provide additional information and answer frequently
asked questions on Historic Preservation in general, Historic Preservation Ordinances, and the
City’s completed Historic Context Statement and Citywide Historic Resources Survey. The
commissioners were also asked to submit any questions they had on the Draft Historic
Preservation Ordinance. Questions were received from four (4) of the five (5) commissioners.
General responses have been provided to each of the commissioners’ questions and it is
expected that further discussion on some of these questions will occur during the December 4th
meeting (Attachment 5).

For informational purposes, a comparison table and summary sheets have been provided of other
San Gabriel Valley cities’ Historic Preservation Ordinances (Attachments 3 and 4). These
attachments are intended to serve as a reference for understanding how surrounding cities have
implemented Historic Preservation Ordinances. The intent is that this supplemental reference
information may help facilitate the Commission’s consideration, discussion, and deliberation on
how to proceed with the Draft Historic Preservation Ordinance.

NEXT STEPS:

During the meeting on December 4th, HRG will provide a presentation that provides an overview
and discussion on the following items:

  Draft Historic Preservation Ordinance

   1. Community Outreach: A summary of the community feedback received on the Draft
  Historic Preservation Ordinance through the City Council District Community Meetings
  and the Draft Historic Preservation Ordinance Questionnaire.

  2. Commissioner Questions & Responses: A summary of the questions received from
  commissioners on the Draft Historic Preservation Ordinance and discussion on
  responses to these questions.

Following the presentation, the Historic Preservation Commission will receive public comment
before proceeding with consideration, discussion, and deliberation on the options for the Draft
Historic Preservation Ordinance (Attachment 6). The four (4) high-level options on how to proceed
include the following:

  1. Discussion Draft: Proceed with the Historic Preservation Ordinance “Discussion Draft”,
  which reflects an approach informed by the most common practices in historic
  preservation regarding protection of historic properties and level of regulation.
  2. Revised Draft: Proceed with a revised Historic Preservation Ordinance modified with
  greater protection for historic resources and higher level of regulation and/or with lesser
  protection for historic resources and lower level of regulation.
  3. Mills Act Only: Do not proceed with the development of a Historic Preservation
  Ordinance; instead develop provisions for administration of the State of California’s Mills
  Act Property Tax Abatement Program (“Mills Act”) only.
  4. No Ordinance: Do not proceed with the development of a local historic preservation
  program (no Historic Preservation Ordinance).

The Historic Preservation Commission will need to come to a consensus in providing staff and
HRG direction on which one (1) of the four (4) options they wish to proceed with. Once the Historic
Preservation Commission has provided this direction, it may or may not be necessary for them to
then consider, discuss, deliberate, and arrive at a consensus on the direction they wish to provide
on the various provision alternatives that can potentially be incorporated into a Draft Historic
Preservation Ordinance. The table of provision alternatives for consideration by the Historic
Preservation Commission is detailed in Attachment 6. Each of the provision alternatives provides
for an option that reflects an approach with either more restrictions, intermediate restrictions, or
less restrictions that can be incorporated into a Historic Preservation Ordinance.

Once the Historic Preservation Commission has provided direction on which option to proceed
with and if necessary, which provision alternatives to incorporate into the draft Historic
Preservation Ordinance, then staff and HRG can move forward with preparing any revisions or
any additional documents necessary for the Historic Preservation Commission to make their
formal recommendation to the Planning Commission and the City Council at their next regular
meeting. Preparation of these revisions or any additional documents cannot proceed until the
Historic Preservation Commission has provided direction on all the requested items.

XXXXX Purpose

 The Alhambra City Council acknowledges that the recognition, preservation, protection, and reuse of
 historic resources are required in the interests of the health, prosperity, safety, social and cultural
 enrichment, general welfare, and economic well-being of the people of Alhambra. Moreover, California
 Government Code § 37361 enables City legislative bodies to “provide for places, buildings, structures,
 works of art, and other objects, having a special character or special historical or aesthetic interest or
 value, special conditions or regulations for their protection, enhancement, perpetuation or use, which
 may include appropriate and reasonable control of the use or appearance of neighboring private
 property within public view, or both.” The designation and preservation of historic resources, and the
 regulation of alterations, additions, repairs, removal, demolition, or new construction to perpetuate the
 historic character of historic resources, is declared to be a public purpose of the City.

 Therefore, the purposes of this Chapter include the following:

 A.  Encourage public knowledge, understanding, and appreciation of the built environment as a
  tangible link to Alhambra’s history;

  B.  Promote the use of historic resources, especially for the education, appreciation, and general
  welfare of the people of Alhambra;

 C.  Enable informed planning decisions regarding the treatment of properties that contribute to the City’s
  character or reflect its historical, cultural, and architectural development;
 D. Provide recommendations to the City Council regarding priorities for preservation, restoration, and
  rehabilitation efforts within the City;
 E.  Safeguard Alhambra’s heritage by protecting resources that reflect elements of the City's historic,
  cultural, social, architectural, and/or archaeological history;
 F.  Deter demolition, misuse, or neglect of designated Historic Landmarks, designated Historic Districts

XXXXX Applicability

  The provisions of this Chapter shall apply to all designated, eligible, or potentially eligible historic resources—
  including buildings, structures, objects, sites, and historic districts—within the City.

XXXXX Definitions

  A. “Alhambra Register of Historic Resources” means the official list of designated historic resources in
  the City. This includes historic resources that have been designated under this Chapter as well as
  those listed in the National Register of Historic Places and/or California Register of Historical
  Resources.

  B.  “Alhambra Inventory of Historic Resources” means the list of historic resources maintained by the City,
  which includes potentially eligible historic resources identified through a citywide historic resources
  survey; eligible historic resources evaluated through a historic resource assessment; and those listed
  in the National Register of Historic Places, California Register of Historical Resources, and/or the
  Alhambra Register of Historic Resources.

  C.  “Archaeological Resource” means any material remains of past human life, activities, or habitation
  which are of historic or prehistoric significance and/or may provide information important to the
  understanding of past human behavior. Such materials include, but are not limited to, artifacts,
  human-modified ecofacts, features, structures or portions/remnants of structures, sites, districts,
  graves, human remains, or any piece of the forgoing items.

  D. “California Environmental Quality Act” (or “CEQA”) refers to the statute and regulations
  applying to public agencies in California as codified in the California Public Resources Code Sections
  21000 through 21178, and Title 14 CCR, Section 753, and Chapter 3, Sections 15000 through
  15387. CEQA applies to all discretionary work proposed to be conducted or approved by a
  California public agency, including private projects requiring discretionary approval.

  E.  “Certificate of Appropriateness” (or “C of A”) refers to the required review prior to issuance of an
  alteration permit to ensure alterations to a designated historic resource, eligible historic resource, or
  potentially eligible historic resource that is determined to be a “historical resource” under CEQA, are
  in compliance with this Chapter and CEQA guidelines.

  F.  “Certificate of Demolition” (or “C of D”) refers to the required review prior to approval of a
  demolition request for a designated historic resource, eligible historic resource, or potentially eligible
  historic resource that is determined to be a “historical resource” under CEQA, are in compliance
  with this Chapter and CEQA guidelines.

  G. “Character-Defining Features” refers to the visual and physical features that give a historic resource
  its identity and distinctive character. They may include its overall form, massing, materials,
  craftsmanship, decorative details, interior spaces and features, and aspects of its site and
  environment.

V.  “Minor Alterations” are defined as:

  a.  Any removal of insignificant exterior features of a designated Historic Landmark, individually

  b.  Any undertaking requiring a permit that does not change substantially the exterior
